title: Integrate and explain the results
goal: Explain how a transaction affects the records, statements, ratios, and final business recommendation.

slides.title: Retrieve the full path from evidence to a decision
slides.takeaway: Explain the links, not just the final numbers.
slides.notes: Use the Harbor case in the handout. Opening balances: Cash $4,000, Equipment $6,000, Notes Payable $3,000, Common Stock $5,000, Retained Earnings $2,000. Six June events; no adjustments or closing entries. Suitable for review around a final exam.

slides.title: Trace one transaction across the records
slides.lead: Harbor · R1 · Complete $2,000 of services on account.
slides.takeaway: The eventual collection is a separate transaction.
slides.notes: The later $1,200 collection leaves an $800 receivable. Revenue is not recognized again.

slides.title: Check the four financial statements together
slides.takeaway: Profit, retained earnings, equity, and cash connect.
slides.notes: Assets: Cash $3,400 + AR $800 + Inventory $800 + Equipment $6,000. Equity: Common Stock $5,000 + RE $3,500. Loan maturity is not supplied, so do not invent a current portion or liquidity ratio. Students derive the figures from the handout first.

slides.title: Explain a profit-versus-cash difference
slides.lead: Net income is positive $1,700, while cash falls $600.
slides.takeaway: Credit sales, unsold inventory, and financing explain the difference.
slides.notes: Operating cash: $1,200 − $300 − $800 = $100. Profit bridge: $1,700 − AR increase $800 − inventory increase $800 = $100. Then subtract principal $500 and dividends $200. No new adjusting entry is needed.

slides.title: Recalculate a ratio after a supported correction

blocks.text: Suppose the $300 utilities payment was recorded as Equipment. Revenue is $2,000.

slides.lead: Find net profit margin before and after correcting the error.
slides.takeaway: A correct ratio formula cannot repair wrong input accounts.
slides.notes: Alternative erroneous version of Harbor; all other events correct. Cash is unchanged by the correction. High margins reflect a small teaching set, not a business benchmark.

slides.title: Evaluate an ethical claim using evidence

blocks.text: The equipment error increased reported profit. Does that prove it was intentional?

slides.takeaway: Separate the accounting effect from its possible explanation.
slides.notes: Discuss misunderstanding, negligence, and intentional manipulation as alternatives to investigate.

blocks.text: No. It establishes a misclassification. Intent needs further evidence, such as repeated patterns, instructions, or altered source records.

slides.title: Defend a recommendation and its limitations

items.heading: Recommendation
items.text: Monitor collections and cash needs before adding fixed payment commitments.

items.heading: Evidence and limit
items.text: Profit is $1,700, but cash fell $600. One month does not establish a trend.

slides.takeaway: State both the reason and the missing evidence.
slides.notes: Pairs defend or challenge the recommendation. Useful evidence includes later collections, forecasts, and loan repayment terms.

slides.title: Complete the cumulative error challenge

rows: $500 principal repayment in operating cash flows

slides.takeaway: Repair the source of each error and update affected outputs.
slides.notes: Independent mistakes, not a combined erroneous statement set. Principal is a cash-flow classification error. Dividend is a statement-placement error with the original Dividends account already correct. Only the first requires the shown journal correction.

rows: Debit Utilities Expense; credit Equipment $300. Profit falls $300.
Move $500 outflow to financing. Total cash change is unchanged.
Exclude from expenses; deduct in retained earnings.

slides.title: Final review of the course learning goals

items: Analyze and journalize transactions from evidence.
Post accounts and check a trial balance.
Prepare and connect the four statements.
Support a recommendation with qualified evidence.

slides.takeaway: Accurate records → connected reports → defensible decisions.
slides.notes: Ask which link students can now explain and which needs practice. No new assessed prerequisite is introduced.
